column3: Primary Theorems 1.5–1.8 and Proposition 1.9 distinguish known codegree/near-codegree cases from the general d-range. Space-barrier construction is already published; no new all-d upper bound or tiling mechanism. Conflicting solved metadata does not close the general conjecture.

Theorem 1.1 explicitly assumes n at least an unspecified N. It supplies the asymptotic regime, not an effective finite remainder certificate; no investment in replaying a known graph-limit result. Small n or uniqueness corrections would not earn discovery credit.

Universal nonexistence outside mu=6,9 above 276 requires classifying primitive strongly regular graphs. Excluding one feasible tuple cannot settle all remaining parameter sets; no bounded certificate family identified.

The referenced Figure and permitted strong contractions are missing from the literal record. Minimality needs exhaustive certified elimination of all smaller graphs, including 12–14 vertices; trivial homology alone does not certify reducibility.

Literal book definition uses k triangles and omits the role of n, while the Ramsey expression depends on both. Need original definition and delta/n quantifier hierarchy before any extremal construction; endpoint arithmetic is not a solution.

Universal list-colorability for every large D requires controlling arbitrary lists under a common-neighbor bound. Greedy D+1 coloring does not give the zeta+epsilon factor; no full-scope probabilistic mechanism.

Digraph D*_m and distinguished component A*_m are not specified. Perron–Frobenius would give simplicity within a primitive component, but neither primitivity nor strict spectral dominance over every other component follows from m<=12.

Construction in Proposition 2 and comparison class of weighted hypersurfaces need primary definitions. Vanishing for one sequence does not establish a universal extremal bound over all quasi-smooth hypersurfaces in every dimension.

Leg multiplicities of lengths 1,2,3 are unbounded. Exact domination-polynomial recurrences could screen finite cases, but no coefficient-ratio or mode-interlacing argument covers all multiplicities; a bounded sweep would not prove unimodality.
Need one absolute D uniformly across all cycle lengths, with n-threshold depending on length. Euler's bound 3n-6 has no required linear deficit; no uniform discharging scheme identified.

Primary Conjecture 2 is genuine; Lemma 1 already reduces any fixed digit fiber to a finite suffix obstruction. The published {4,4,7} witness and e=8 test are reproduced only as a known instance, not universal credit. No bound on e for arbitrary digit multiplicities.

Scale-preserving fat-shattering is sensitive to unrestricted thresholds and Log convention. Ordinary VC union bounds do not directly yield the exact gamma-scale inequality; need primary hypotheses and no complete bridge identified.

Record contains an unrelated-sounding Bohman–Holzman refutation quotation. No literal correspondence packing definition or primary body checked; do not treat the status annotation as either resolution or novelty clearance.

Equality requires optimal equivariant covers for every finite group and every dimension. Existing two-sided interval alone gives no universal construction; trivial-group/dimension convention corrections are ineligible.

Minimum degree and forbidden induced cycle family do not bound graph order. A full result needs a uniform differential/discharging argument for every k; exact optimization on a few graphs cannot close it.

Literal equality 15n/7 for every n conflicts with integrality, and n=3 has exact value 3. Primary Theorem 1(iii) lists bounds; disjoint seven-vertex examples cannot give equality in every order. This is a domain/rounding issue and earns zero credit.

Source Theorem 1(v) gives upper/lower bounds rather than the literal piecewise equality. Small maximal planar witnesses do not settle all n; no exact upper-bound induction identified. Definition/order corrections receive zero credit.

Requires extremal independent-set bound for every flag sphere in every dimension. Suspension gives constructions but no all-dimensional upper bound; small-dimensional cases or feasibility-domain fixes are ineligible.

Literal record restricts S to odd primes, making x=3 trivial on infinitely many diagonal pairs. Primary instead includes 1 in S and has a bullet a=1; its twin-prime equivalence uses distinct p1<p2. Source-domain and quantifier mismatches preclude credit; no general prime-pair mechanism identified.

The quantified simultaneous bounds for all k strengthen ordinary path partition. Record's solved quotation concerns supporting undirected results and does not prove arbitrary digraphs. No full-scope partition mechanism; status not trusted.
All squarefree polynomials of arbitrary degree are quantified. Low-degree/abc-conditional results do not give an unconditional full-degree sieve; no local obstruction or new construction identified.
Need exact genetic code order, smallest gee convention and involution defining coindex. Existing lower bound does not supply an equivariant upper obstruction for arbitrary generic length vector.
Blocking odd cycle orientation is only referenced, not fully defined. Necessity via a forbidden cycle does not imply sufficiency for arbitrary induced subdigraphs and every maximum stable set.

Primary Conjecture 20 exactly matches the stated residue classes. Section 4.1 Theorem 17 addresses different classes (14,22,29 mod31) and cannot settle this complement; a finite code table through 256 does not prove all lengths. Need all-length distance upper bound under self-orthogonality.

For every n with exact degeneracy k is infeasible when n<=k; graph-size rounding also matters. Treat as domain correction, not refutation credit. Intended large-n lower bound requires a new feedback-set construction beyond tournament estimates.

Primary v4 Theorem 1.3 states exactly pi_2(K4^-)=1/4. Its proof uses Lemma 2.8 rational flag-algebra identity and nonnegative evaluations; body read, computational matrices/Appendix not replayed. Already public full-scope theorem, no discovery credit.

Finite-looking 13-point target lacks literal coordinates and exact admissible extension rules. Need source configuration first and a complete geometric search or obstruction; arbitrary point enumeration has no finite completeness certificate yet.
Same missing base configuration as 353050; a 16-point example search cannot certify universal strict <20. Need finite reduction and all real-coordinate degeneracies, not merely a lattice sweep.
All planar graphs quantified; C5 proves only sharpness of a possible bound. No universal reducible-configuration/extension argument for odd neighborhood parity identified.

Arbitrary integer polynomial includes degeneracies (zero values or fixed higher powers); literal claim needs source restrictions. Retained v3 proof of Theorem 2 uses Henriot bounds with discriminant factor, not the unrestricted displayed conjecture; exact older formulation/scope unqualified. No wording-refutation credit.

LCD tie-breaking and SCD/BCD/TCD alternatives require primary definitions and Theorem heavy. Trying linear extensions of a few fences cannot prove existence for all beta; no stable inductive extension rule.

Only intermediate n remains beyond quoted known ranges. A finite interval for each k is still unbounded as k grows; k=1 endpoint convention issues are not substantive discoveries. No all-k rainbow extremal mechanism.

Interval enclosure requires certified universal lower bound and explicit upper witness under the actual overlap functional. Floating convex-program optimum is neither certificate; no rational dual with full functional constraints identified.

Literal definition suppresses maximization over great-circle arrangements. Coxeter tilings give lower witnesses only; proving optimality needs a global spherical bound, not verification of three symmetric examples.

Literal chi-bounded definition and dichromatic symbol are malformed. Need primary forbidden-induced-digraph convention and bounding parameter before investigation; no universal directed Gyarfás–Sumner mechanism inferred from record.

Retained v2 Theorem 3 gives E[F]<=n(H_{2mu}+1), which implies O(n log(2mu)); Theorem 7 proof inspected in part. Published rotation-system bound subsumes target, no new credit. Complete process lemmas/dependencies not audited.

max(uv) versus max(u,v), mixed one-base/multibase Upsilon notation, and unspecified Phi sequence prevent exact scope qualification. Chinese remainder intuition alone cannot resolve the threshold definition.

Refuted annotation appears to concern another conjecture, not automatically this high-girth assertion. Need original large-degree quantifiers; no construction produces arbitrary prescribed girth and minimum degree in every high-degree graph.

Primary odd covers are XOR sums of bicliques, not arbitrary binary Gram representations. Theorem 6.4 already constructs residues +-1 mod8; Conjecture 7.2 retains 3,5. General rank lower bound is insufficient to construct covers at the lower endpoint. No new all-residue construction.

Need curves of every sufficiently large genus for each fixed q,gamma, with exact gonality and all gamma(q+1) rational points. One cover family or infinitely many genera cannot meet the universal eventual-genus quantifier.

All connected bounded-degree graphs quantified; odd-degree vertices are easy but even-degree neighborhoods obstruct greedy coloring. No recoloring invariant handles every Delta and graph; finite search cannot establish universal bound.
Unique neighborhood color is stronger than odd multiplicity. A result for odd colorings or subcubic graphs alone does not imply all Delta+1 PCF bound. No full-scope extension mechanism.

Temporal arc-disjoint paths do not automatically pack temporally respecting spanning trees via static Edmonds theorem. Need simultaneous temporal compatibility under n/2 connectivity; no short uncrossing argument identified.

Need generic non-semi-algebraicity of convex cells, not just transcendental appearance of equations (which does not imply that property). No exact analytic section with provably nonalgebraic boundary and generic persistence identified.

Primary Section 7 already cites DDLP Proposition 8 for {1,3,2c}. Theorem 19 proves an extension without 3, not Family A. Adding moves can alter mex in either direction; no all-heap/all-extra-cuts nim-set containment certificate. Prior/successor and registry gates remain HOLD before any substantial proof attempt.

Literal record explicitly says theorem already proved; no rediscovery investment. Primary successor proof not fetched or replayed here, so this is reported public-resolution exclusion only, not independently certified theorem coverage.

Primary Problem 1.8 asks uniform c across all F. Theorem 1.6 supplies c<=4 only for almost bipartite F; transferring it to general F has no identified bridge. Existing lower constructions do not show unbounded c(F).

Primary cover-degree convention matters: H uses independent fibers whereas full covers may include clique fibers. Constant 4 in Theorem 1.12 does not establish 1+epsilon even under triangle-freeness; no probabilistic sharpening mechanism supplied.

Almost-all claim requires density tending to one in a specified random-graph regime. Enumeration through ten vertices or a rare cospectral pair cannot prove or refute it; no asymptotic spectral reconstruction mechanism.

Conditional almost-all statement on graphs having nonbacktracking mates needs denominator asymptotics as well as Laplacian uniqueness. A regular cospectral family gives instances only, not positive conditional density; no full-scope counting argument.
